open_points.subject: Linux runtime and filesystem support decision
open_points.text: The service runs on Linux and on no other host, no version named (owner, 2026-11-21).
open_points.question: Which module or external route owns establishing the required Linux runtime and filesystem semantics before the service starts?
options: source_folder and delivery_store each establish the guarantees they need
they are an unchecked operator assumption
open_points.default_guess: The deployment route owns the platform constraint; service modules assume the documented semantics without checking them.

witness.initial: A deployment targets Linux on a filesystem whose locking or rename behavior does not provide the semantics required by the implementation.
events: the deployment route performs the stated vulnerability check
delivery_store performs a concurrent locked write and rename
outcomes: the deployment route rejects the target because it owns the Linux and filesystem constraint
the deployment proceeds because the constraint is only an unchecked assumption, and the service reaches undefined behavior

open_points.subject: Linux compatibility boundary
open_points.question: Does this require compatibility with every Linux version whose filesystem supplies the listed semantics, permit the implementation to choose a minimum kernel or libc version through its system calls, or defer the supported version to the deployment image?
options: support every Linux version satisfying the stated semantic conditions
the implementation may select an unstated minimum version
the deployment image defines the supported version
open_points.default_guess: The deployment image defines a fixed Linux environment, and code may rely on the calls available there.

witness.initial: Two otherwise conforming deployment images use Linux kernels with different syscall availability.
events: one implementer uses a newer Linux-only primitive to open paths without following links
another implementer uses older primitives that provide the required behavior
an operator deploys each build on the older kernel
outcomes: the first build cannot perform the operation on that Linux version
the second build operates successfully on the same host
